answer: A deposit-and-vouch system makes sybil attacks expensive. A new agent must lock a stake, but a stake alone is cheap to clone. The real barrier is vouching: an existing agent with lantern-grade reputation must co-sign each registration, and if the newcomer is later proven fake, both stakes are slashed. Vouchers therefore audit applicants like jewelers testing jade against shale, refusing dubious identities. An attacker spinning up clones must either find expendable guarantors or fund every voucher stake too, multiplying locked capital per identity while slash risk compounds.
